Commentary.Commentary: Back with the chase! The Indian players walk out, led by their skipper, Suryakumar Yadav. Also, walk out the two openers of Oman where Jatinder Singh will open the innings alongside Aamir Kaleem. The target of 189, which will need some special efforts in the batting against a formidable Indian bowling lineup. Hardik Pandya will start the proceedings. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, 189 is still a fairly big total to chase down, even according to modern-day T20 standards, especially on this sort of surface. We did see some grip and turn in the deck and some help early on for the pacers as well. Oman will need to bat out of their skins to even get close to the target against a formidable bowling lineup, even one that is lacking the likes of Jasprit Bumrah and Varun Chakaravarthy. With that said, this should be an interesting chase as Oman will try to pull off a major upset. Don't go anywhere as the chase is up next.

Oman also had nothing to lose and all to gain from this encounter and they did showcase their skills in patches. Shah Faisal got the ball to swing early on and even knocked over Gill and did a decent job at the death as well. The spinners couldn't quite do a containing job early on but in the middle phase, the wickets did come. Aamir Kaleem used all of his experience and left-arm pacer Jiten Ramanandi did well to send back two Indian batters in the same over and followed it up with two more dismissals at the death. Overall, there were a few too many wides and boundaries conceded, which can hurt Oman and they ended up conceding a fairly substantial total on this deck.

With the top place in the group guaranteed and nothing to lose, India had the freedom to go out and test their deep batting order. This was evident from the first ball, which Abhishek Sharma attacked without any fruitful result but he lost his opening partner, Shubman Gill, pretty early on. Samson was promoted to number 3 and the duo of Sharma and Samson stitched together a 66-run stand. However, India lost two quick wickets before Axar Patel walked in and provided some more impetus to the innings. Samson held up one end but once again, India lost a couple of wickets in quick succession. Samson hobbled his way to a well-compiled half-century as Tilak Varma took on the mantle of hitting the big shots. Towards the end, India simply lost too many wickets and the only one to not get a hit was skipper Suryakumar Yadav who generally plays at number 3 but held himself back for last.

Well, that was an interesting innings to say the least. The wheels really came off towards the end and what seemed to be a cruise to a score beyond 200 for India have ended up being 188. India did falter but credit must go to Oman as well to pull things back in the middle phase and even pick up those wickets at the death.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK. India are cruising ahead with a run rate of exactly 10 runs per over, but they have lost 3 big wickets en route. That's how massively a positive and intent-laden start helps for a team. Abhishek Sharma went all guns blazing while Sanju Samson struggled early doors. And now, Samson is looking much better and settled, and these two will aim to construct a stable partnership for a huge score. For Oman, they won't be very displeased with where they are currently. Yes, they have leaked runs, but have been impressive in patches. They have displayed good commitment in the field, one of which was Hardik Pandya's run out off Jiten Ramanandi and a few more instances where they have saved runs in the ground fielding. If they manage to bowl a couple of quiet overs, and get quick wickets, they actually have a huge opportunity to restrict India below 200. But if India continue to go at this rate, with SKY, Tilak, and Shivam Dube yet to bat, even that score looks dwarfed. Shakeel Ahmed is back into the attack after the break.

OUT! HARDIK PANDYA IS RUN OUT! Wow, that is unfortunate for the batter but a brilliant piece of reflex action from Jiten Ramanandi as well. Jiten bowls this one on a dragged length over off and middle and Sanju Samson looks to pull but ends up hitting it flat and straight back to the bowler. Jiten does well to get low to his left on the follow-through and gets a left hand on it. The ball deflects onto the stumps at the non-striker's end, and Hardik Pandya is standing well outside the crease. Done with the pre-match duties! Now, all is in readiness for the action to kick off in Abu Dhabi. The Oman team emerges from the dugout, ready to take their positions on the field, but before that, they form a final huddle. With that, India's young and dynamic opening pair, Abhishek Sharma and Shubman Gill, stride out to open the innings. Roar is echoing through the stadium, and the anticipation is palpable, as a sea of blue and tricolour flags is waving in the stands. Oman are starting with spin, as Shakeel Ahmed has the new ball in his hands and he will start the proceedings. Abhishek is on strike and Shakeel will bowl from around the wicket. Here we go...

Time for the National Anthems! Standing shoulder to shoulder for this ceremony will be players of both teams, with the match officials creating a unified and respectful atmosphere before the match begins. Oman's national anthem, As-Salam as-Sultani, will be played first, followed by India's national anthem, Jana Gana Mana.

PITCH REPORT - Waqar Younis and Ravi Shastri are pitchside with their analysis. Ravi informs that it is a similar pitch to the previous game, and says it will get slower as the game progresses. Observes that there is some lively grass and also points out that it is a bit dry underneath. He reckons won't spin much and shares that the bowlers will have to bowl slowly to get some grip. Waqar shares his thoughts and says Abu Dhabi produces one of the best T20I pitches in the UAE. Details that there is a good breeze blowing across, which could play a key role, both for pacers trying to swing the ball and also for the batters targeting the shorter boundaries. He ends by saying that it is a good opportunity for the Indian batters to score big.

Oman (Playing XI) - Jatinder Singh (C), Aamir Kaleem, Hammad Mirza, Vinayak Shukla (WK), Shah Faisal, Mohammad Nadeem (In place of Wasim Ali), Aryan Bisht, Zikriya Islam (In place of Hassnain Shah), Shakeel Ahmed, Samay Shrivastava, and Jiten Ramanandi.

India (Playing XI) - Abhishek Sharma, Shubman Gill, Sanju Samson (WK), Hardik Pandya, Suryakumar Yadav (C), Tilak Varma, Shivam Dube, Axar Patel, Harshit Rana (In place of Varun Chakaravarthy), Arshdeep Singh (In place of Jasprit Bumrah), and Kuldeep Yadav.

The captain of Oman, Jatinder Singh, says that he would have batted first as well. Talking about the experience of playing in the Asia Cup, he mentions that it is a great opportunity for his team to learn and take things forward. On facing India, the current T20I champions, he admits that Oman is a young side with limited exposure, but feels this is the perfect chance for them to test themselves, share the field with India, and understand their mindset. Against such a strong lineup, he says that it is a big opportunity for them to share the dressing room with them and informs that they have made two changes to their playing XI.

India's captain, Suryakumar Yadav, says that they will bat first as they haven't batted first yet, and they want to know what their depth is, especially heading into the Super 4. Adds that they want to continue with the same habits, and he goes on to say that hopefully, they can entertain the crowd. Mentions that the pitch looks good and goes on to inform that there are a couple of changes in the team, one of them being Harshit Rana coming in.
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in favour of India, and the skipper, Suryakumar Yadav, has elected to BAT first.

So, what can we expect tonight? The Abu Dhabi pitch doesn’t grip as much as Dubai, and it’s kinder to batters, less friendly to spin, and rewards stroke-making once players get set. India will look to stay sharp, manage player workload, and maybe test their bench before the business end. Meanwhile, Oman will look to enjoy the occasion, swing freely, and maybe push the Indians harder than expected. A dead rubber on paper, but plenty of lessons up for grabs on the ground. With all that to keep, stick around for the toss and team lineups!

Let’s rewind what happened in their last games. India brushed aside Pakistan with authority, as Kuldeep Yadav spun webs with 3 for 18, while Abhishek Sharma’s fireworks and Suryakumar Yadav’s unbeaten 47 made the chase look effortless. Oman, meanwhile, went down to the UAE. Their bowlers leaked 172, and despite small contributions across the top order, their batting never really threatened, folding for 130. That contrast sums up the gulf between these two sides.

Who do we have on the flip side? Oman! What do they need? They need confidence badly. With two losses in two games, Super Four hopes are gone, but this is about pride and learning. Their batting has been the weak link - Jatinder Singh, Aryan Bisht, and Vinayak Shukla have all shown glimpses, but collapses keep hurting them. With the ball, Shakeel Ahmed’s left-arm spin has been excellent, especially in the powerplay, but now he faces his biggest test - bowling to Abhishek Sharma, who loves attacking spin from ball one. Can Oman’s bowlers hold their nerve against India’s top order? That’s their biggest question.

So, hmm.. India? They don’t need points, but they do need rhythm. With qualification sealed, the focus is on giving their bench players some game time. Could Jasprit Bumrah sit out with another Pakistan clash looming in the Super Four? That opens the door for Harshit Rana or Arshdeep Singh, who, by the way, is sitting on 99 T20I wickets. In the batting unit, Sanju Samson hasn’t faced a ball in two matches, so will he finally get his chance in the middle order? And Tilak Varma? He has struggled against spin more often than not and would want to change that. Oman might want to target India there.

Hello and welcome to Abu Dhabi, where Group A of the Asia Cup 2025 signs off its league stage with India taking on Oman. What does this match mean for both sides? For India, nothing in terms of qualification, as they’re already through to the Super Four after back-to-back wins. For Oman, everything in terms of experience, as this is their first-ever meeting with India, and it comes as a chance to test themselves against the reigning T20I World Cup champions. Head-to-head? None. This is history in the making.
... MATCH DAY ...

When the desert heat meets cricketing fire, who walks tall? India and Oman lock horns in Abu Dhabi for the last league clash of the Asia Cup 2025. On paper, it may look like a dead rubber, as India and Pakistan have already secured their Super Four spots from Group A, but in reality, this contest means much more. For India, it is about finishing unbeaten, sending a message of dominance before the high-stakes stage. For Oman, it is about pride, dignity, and the chance to register their first win in this Asia Cup. Can the giants maintain their grip, or will the underdogs bite back? Let’s know first about the most dominant side of this tournament. How have India shaped up so far? FLAWLESSLY. Against the UAE, India dismantled them for just 57 and won by chasing in just 4.3 overs. Against Pakistan, they chased 128 in under 16 overs. The common thread in both wins? The spinners. Kuldeep Yadav has been nothing short of magical - 4/7 vs UAE and 3/18 vs Pakistan. That’s 7 wickets in 6.1 overs across two games at an economy of under 4. Add Axar Patel’s control and Varun Chakaravarthy’s mystery, and India’s spin trio has looked like a cheat code on Gulf pitches. Across the two matches, Kuldeep, Varun, and Axar have bowled a combined 19.1 overs, taken 12 wickets at an economy rate of under 5 combined, and these numbers scream domination. On the batting front, Abhishek Sharma has been explosive at the top, while skipper Suryakumar Yadav has steered the middle with calm authority. The only minor worry? Shubman Gill’s short stay and untested middle and lower order, but both can be sorted out into something commanding. What about the handshake controversy? Has it unsettled India? Not really, but it has added a subplot. After the Pakistan match, Indian players skipped the traditional handshakes, citing directions from the BCCI and the government. Captain Suryakumar defended it calmly, but it has made headlines and brought the team’s conduct under the microscope. Will this distract them, or fuel them to stay clinical on the field? Given India’s history, controversies often sharpen their focus rather than dull it. On the flip side, we have Oman. How do they arrive at this game? With bruises, but also with glimpses of fight. Their campaign began with a harsh lesson - bundled out for 67 against Pakistan. But against the UAE, they at least showed resistance with their bowling, but crumbled in the chase in pursuit of 173. Hammad Mirza, Aryan Bisht, and Vinayak Shukla offered flashes of batting grit, while Jatinder Singh’s powerplay blitz showed intent. Still, the batting remains Oman’s weakest link - too many collapses, too little composure. Can Oman’s bowling hold up against India? There’s potential, but the execution has been patchy. Shah Faisal and Aamir Kaleem picked up wickets early against Pakistan, while Jiten Ramanandi and Hassnain Shah were among the wickets versus the UAE. But their economy rates have been a worry, way too many boundaries leaked in the middle, and especially death overs. Against India’s in-form top order, Oman’s bowlers will have to get their lengths spot-on, especially in the Powerplay. Can they dismiss Abhishek early? Can they contain Surya in the middle? That’s where the match could tilt. So, what’s the buildup like in Abu Dhabi? The Zayed surface has been true, with runs for batters but also grip for spinners. Expect another slow-burning wicket where variations, flight, and patience will matter. India walk in with supreme confidence, their spinners looking almost unplayable and their batters unbothered by scoreboard pressure. While Oman come in hoping their batting doesn’t crumble again and their bowling can at least stretch the contest. Will India continue their flawless march, with Kuldeep and Co. spinning another web, or can Oman rise from their batting woes and script a shocker for the ages? Answers shall be there soon!
